name: Rattanakosin Kingdom (Siam)
native: รัตนโกสินทร์ (Rattanakosin)

predecessors.name: Thonburi Kingdom
predecessors.text: the Thonburi Kingdom, ended by 'Deposition of Taksin: 1 April 1782'; 'Chaophraya Chakri ascended the throne as King Rama I' (Thonburi page)

successors.name: Kingdom of Thailand
successors.text: Siam after the revolution of 24 June 1932, which ended the absolute monarchy

ledger.x: 1782: Vientiane is a Siamese tributary kingdom.
1782: Luang Phrabang is a Siamese tributary kingdom, inherited from Thonburi (tributary since the capture of Vientiane in 1779 per the Thonburi page).
1782: Champasak is a Siamese tributary kingdom, inherited from Thonburi (Champasak captured in 1778, tributary after 1779 per the Thonburi page).
1782: Lanna (Chiang Mai) is a Siamese tributary.
1782: Rama I founds the Rattanakosin Kingdom at Bangkok.
1782: the royal seat moves from Thonburi on the west bank of the Chao Phraya to Bang Makok (Bangkok) on the east bank, for better defense; the city pillar was consecrated on 21 April 1782.
1786: Pattani is conquered and brought under Siamese rule (1786: Pattani was conquered and brought under Siamese rule).
1786: the northern Malay sultanate of Kelantan is a Siamese tributary again.

1786: the northern Malay sultanate of Terengganu is a Siamese tributary again ('Siam only resumed real political control over the Northern Malay sultanates in 1786'); the Rattanakosin page lists Terengganu among its tributary polities.
1793: After the Battle of Tavoy, Siam ceded the Tenasserim Coast to Burma, 'for perpetuity' (now Tanintharyi).
1794: Siam takes north-western Cambodia under direct rule.
1821: Siam annexes Kedah.
1827: the Lao rebellion reaches Siam.
1828: the rebellion is crushed.
1828: the Kingdom of Vientiane is abolished.
1828: Vientiane's lands pass to Siam.
1833: Siam invades Cambodia and Hà Tiên to oust the Vietnamese.
1834: the Siamese withdraw.
1839: Perlis becomes a separate Siamese-supervised state: 1839: Kedah was divided into four states (Setul, Kubang Pasu, Perlis, and Kedah proper).
1841: Siam intervenes in Cambodia again.
1842: Kedah is returned to its sultan.
1842: the restored Kedah stays a Siamese tributary.
1847: Cambodia comes under joint suzerainty.
1848: Siam invests Ang Duong as King of Cambodia (19 January 1848).
1867: Siam gives up Cambodia but keeps Battambang and Siem Reap.
1893: France occupies Chanthaburi as a guarantee: As guarantees, France temporarily occupied Chanthaburi.
1893: the Franco-Siamese crisis over the east bank of the Mekong.
1893: Siam cedes the east bank of the Mekong to France.
1893: the crisis ends with the treaty of 3 October 1893; the east bank is French from then on.
1893: Luang Phrabang leaves Siamese suzerainty with the cession of the east bank (3 October 1893).
1893: Champasak leaves Siamese suzerainty with the cession of the east bank (3 October 1893); its right-bank part is ceded in 1904 (Rattanakosin page).
1899: Lanna's tributary status ends.
1899: Siam annexes Lanna.

1904: France gives Chanthaburi back: Siam ceded 'Mluprey, Champasak and Sainyabuli' in exchange for France's abandonment of Chanthaburi (Rattanakosin page); the 1904 treaty page says France agreed to return Chanthaburi to Siam.
1904: Siam cedes the right bank of the Mekong.
1904: in exchange for Chanthaburi the French seized Phatchantakhirikhet and Dan Sai from Siam; the Franco-Siamese War page adds that France held Chanthaburi and Trat until 1907.
1907: Siam cedes Inner Cambodia to France.
1907: France withdraws from Trat and Dan Sai under the treaty of 23 March 1907 (France agreed to withdraw from Trat and Dan Sai); the 1908 shape regains Trat.
1909: Siam transfers its suzerainty over Kedah to Britain.
1909: Siam transfers its suzerainty over Perlis to Britain (Anglo-Siamese Treaty, effective 9 July 1909).
1909: Siam transfers its suzerainty over Kelantan to Britain (Anglo-Siamese Treaty, effective 9 July 1909).
1909: Siam transfers its suzerainty over Terengganu (Tringganu) to Britain (Anglo-Siamese Treaty, effective 9 July 1909).
1932: the Siamese revolution of 24 June ends the absolute monarchy and with it the Rattanakosin Kingdom as the page frames it; Cliopatria continues the same land as the Kingdom of Thailand.

wars.name: Nine Armies' War
wars.outcome: Siam beat back the Burmese invasions; no border changed on the pages opened.

wars.name: Burmese invasion of Thalang (Phuket)
wars.outcome: The last Burmese incursion into Siamese territory; no border changed.

wars.name: Siamese conquest of Kedah
wars.outcome: Kedah annexed by Siam in November 1821; the sultan lived 20 years in exile and was restored in 1842.

wars.name: Lao rebellion (1826-1828)
wars.outcome: Siamese victory: the Kingdom of Vientiane abolished and its lands put under direct Siamese provincial administration; Champasak and Luang Phrabang remained vassals.

wars.name: Siamese-Vietnamese War (1833-1834)
wars.outcome: Vietnamese victory: Siam withdrew by April 1834; Vietnam set up Trấn Tây Province in Cambodia in November 1835.

wars.name: Siamese-Vietnamese War (1841-1845)
wars.outcome: Stalemate: agreement in January 1847, Ang Duong crowned, Cambodia under joint Siamese-Vietnamese suzerainty; the Vietnamese withdrew in mid-1847 and Siam in April 1848.

wars.name: Franco-Siamese War
wars.outcome: French victory: treaty of 3 October 1893; Siam cedes the east bank of the Mekong; France occupies Chanthaburi (and later Trat) until 1904-1907.

certainty.note: A mandala-style realm of direct provinces and tributary kingdoms; frontiers with the Lao states, Cambodia, Lanna and the Malay sultanates are approximate.
